transcript: Alright folks, here's my review of masquerade the new immersive Phantom of the opera experience. I have five main takeaways and then I'll share my overall impressions this is a big event. it's massive in scope and extremely well thought out. the building housing this production is huge with multiple floors and every room, prop, and costume is finely detailed. With just how intentional everything is and how committed the production is to transporting you into the world of the Phantom, it totally felt like something worthy of getting dressed up for, even with yesterday's 90 degree heat. The whole thing just felt really epic from start to finish. the vibes are immaculate. the energy of the audience was a huge part of what made the experience memorable for me, which can always be the case with theatre but I think it's augmented here by the intimate nature of the experience and the fact that you're in a small group of about 60 people. and it's still early in the run so I think pretty much everyone going right now has to be in the know about it in some way, making them more invested than maybe your average audience member. I could definitely tell how much people love Phantom and that made this even more special. it was more structured than I expected. with my frame of reference being Sleep No More which was mostly a free roaming experience, this was a prescribed, meticulously planned experience where you're physically led through the story ensuring that you get the plot. I think this makes a lot of sense with it being a musical too, because you obviously wouldn't wanna miss out on any of the songs. This is quite an impressive logistical feat for everyone involved. when you enter the performance, you and your group have a specific timeslot and these timeslots are scheduled 15 minutes apart from one another. considering we never saw or heard another group while we were going through it, they must have the traffic and the timing of this down to a science. I'd be so curious to see all the spreadsheets that were made to organize this. the material is well taken care of, but some compromises definitely had to be made. it's a tall order to adapt such an iconic story and score for a completely different theatrical form. I think no matter how you do it, you won't be able to fully please everyone, but this production does a pretty good job maintaining the key plot points and the gravity of the music even without live orchestrations. also, the cast was great. Raoul was super hot which always helps, but I digress. with great performances and strong sound design, the music still hits and I think the story comes through enough. overall, I thought it was amazing and super impressive. I certainly have thoughts on specific ways the production could’ve or should’ve handled some of the material, but that's all just a matter of personal preference and I think they did a good job catering to a wide array of people who’ll have various preexisting relationships with the musical. as far as price point, I'm always gonna vouch for making theater accessible, but I gotta say, I thought this was worth the price. I paid $200 for my ticket which was pretty steep, but felt justified after I saw just how much had to go into this production. I don't wanna spoil anything, but it kinda seemed like the budget was nonexistent with how detailed and opulent it was. that said, I hope they implement some sort of rush or lottery system at some point, and I think that's possible as I can see this running for a long time. by nature, this is the kind of thing where no two people are gonna have the exact same experience, so if you've attended and you wanna sound off in the comments, I'd love to hear your thoughts. with that, another program for my collection
classificationReason: Creator gives detailed review of masquerade immersive Phantom experience with specific observations about production elements
